title: Delhi University students march for women's safety after alleged gang rape
seoTitle: Delhi students' marches for women's safety

tea.why: A 17-year-old was allegedly gang-raped in Delhi's Aastha Kunj Park on Sept 21 by men posing as police officers.
tea.want: Safer streets and transit instead of hostel curfews, and strict action in sexual violence cases.
tea.changed: Oct 3: students marched outside Gargi and Kamala Nehru colleges; Congress leader Priyanka Gandhi backed them.

summary: Students from Delhi University colleges, including Lady Shri Ram College, have held a series of marches since late September after the alleged gang rape of a 17-year-old girl in Aastha Kunj Park on September 21. According to reports, three men who posed as police officers are accused; all three were arrested. The September 28 march at the university's Arts faculty was the third solidarity march, and students have since marched outside Gargi College and Kamala Nehru College. Their demand has shifted from campus rules to public safety: better-lit streets, safer transit and accountability, rather than curfews for women. Congress leader Priyanka Gandhi Vadra publicly praised the students on October 3.
demands: Safer public spaces and transit instead of curfews
Strict action in sexual violence cases
response: Police arrested the three accused in the Aastha Kunj case, The Daily Star reported. No other official response is reported in the sources.

crowd.text: hundreds of LSR students joined the Sept 28 march, per The Hindu

updates.text: Third solidarity march at Delhi University; hundreds of LSR students marched towards Moolchand.
Students marched outside Gargi and Kamala Nehru colleges; Priyanka Gandhi Vadra backed the protests.
Reports said the protests were continuing to grow alongside the anti-CEC demonstrations.
